doc.title: Yu-Gi-Oh! Tier List
doc.summary: The Yu-Gi-Oh! tier list, updated October 30, 2026: Angelechy, Power Patron / Elfnote and 3 more lead TCG, and Blitzclique and Angelechy lead Genesys. Ranked from 164,971 YGO Omega ladder matches.

blocks.md:
This Yu-Gi-Oh! tier list ranks the strongest decks on the YGO Omega ranked ladders by their results, using data through October 29, 2026. **Angelechy** (10.6%, 55.2%), **Power Patron / Elfnote** (1.0%, 55.7%), **Radiant Typhoon** (2.9%, 54.9%), **Elfnote** (4.4%, 54.7%) and **Blitzclique** (3.9%, 54.5%) share TCG Tier 1. **Blitzclique** (4.5%, 60.7%) and **Angelechy** (3.3%, 60.4%) share Genesys Tier 1.

A tier here measures **how well a deck wins**, not how much it is played, and a small sample can't lift a deck to the top. For what moved this week, read the [latest meta report](/wiki/yu-gi-oh-meta-report-october-30-2026); for the numbers as they change, the [live statistics page](/statistics).

blocks.text: Which decks are underplayed and overplayed?

blocks.md:
Popularity and results don't always agree. The underplayed decks reach the top two tiers on a small share of the meta, though the people playing them may be specialists, so treat them as leads to test. The overplayed decks are among the ten most played without reaching those tiers.

- **TCG underplayed:** Power Patron / Elfnote (1.0% of the meta, 55.7% wins), Power Patron (1.0% of the meta, 53.4% wins) and Power Patron / Light and Darkness Ritual (1.2% of the meta, 53.0% wins)
- **TCG overplayed:** HERO (5.1% of the meta, 51.7% wins), Sky Striker (4.8% of the meta, 48.7% wins) and Light and Darkness Ritual (4.0% of the meta, 52.1% wins)
- **Genesys underplayed:** Centur-Ion / Angelechy (0.6% of the meta, 59.7% wins), Artmage (0.7% of the meta, 59.9% wins) and Angelechy / Ashtra (0.8% of the meta, 59.9% wins)
- **Genesys overplayed:** Hecahands (2.6% of the meta, 54.0% wins), HERO (2.3% of the meta, 50.2% wins) and Dragon Ruler (2.3% of the meta, 50.5% wins)

Generic Main Deck cards seen across at least two archetypes, by share of deck-games. In TCG, [Ash Blossom & Joyous Spring](/wiki/card/14558127) shows up in 89.1% of decks, and [Mulcharmy Fuwalos](/wiki/card/42141493) shows up in 83.5% of decks.
In Genesys, [Skull Meister](/wiki/card/67750322) shows up in 28.4% of decks, and [Ghost Ogre & Snow Rabbit](/wiki/card/59438930) shows up in 27.1% of decks.

Every number comes from ranked matches played on [YGO Omega](/wiki/ygo-omega-wiki), the same data behind our [statistics page](/statistics). Nothing is voted on or picked by hand.

These are **power tiers**: they rank results. The tiers on the statistics page measure something else, how much a deck is played, so the same deck can sit in different tiers on the two pages.

**Each deck gets a score, the Wilson lower bound of its win rate.** That is the low end of the range its true win rate is likely in, so a deck needs both a good record and enough games to score well: 60% over 500 games scores below 58% over 5,000. A tier is how far a deck's score sits below the best deck on its ladder:

| Tier | Points below the best score |
|---|---|
| Tier 1 | Up to 1 |
| Tier 2 | 1 to 3 |
| Tier 3 | 3 to 6 |
| Tier 4 | 6 to 9 |

The best deck is always Tier 1. Decks past the last band stay outside the tiers. A deck needs at least 0.5% of the meta and 10 players to be ranked at all, because the score corrects for few games, not for few pilots.

- **Meta share** is the deck's share of deck-games. Each game counts once per player, and mirror matches count.
- **Win rate** leaves mirror matches out, because a mirror always wins exactly half. The ± is its 95% confidence interval.
- **Decks** are grouped by the archetypes they run, so a hybrid counts apart from pure builds.
- **Seasons:** each ladder has its own season, so TCG and Genesys cover different date ranges.

blocks.title: What this list can't tell you
blocks.md: This is ladder play on a simulator, not tournament results. Players of every level are in it, and a deck played mostly by specialists can score above what it would do in most hands. It shows what wins on the ladder, which is not always what wins a premier event.

items.q: What is the best Yu-Gi-Oh! deck right now?
items.md: On the TCG ladder, Angelechy, with a 55.2% win rate at 10.6% of the meta. It has the strongest win rate once sample size is counted.

items.q: What is the best Genesys deck right now?
items.md: Blitzclique, with a 60.7% win rate at 4.5% of the meta. It has the strongest win rate once sample size is counted.

items.q: Is this tier list based on tournament results?
items.md: No. It comes from ranked ladder matches on YGO Omega. That gives a far larger sample than tournaments, but it reflects ladder play, not premier events.

By score: the Wilson lower bound of a deck's win rate, which rewards a good record over many games. Tiers 1 to 4 are up to 1, 3, 6, 9 points below the best deck. Decks under 0.5% of the meta or 10 players aren't ranked.

items.q: Does a popular deck get a higher tier?
items.md: No. Tiers follow results. HERO holds 5.1% of the TCG meta and sits in Tier 3, while Power Patron / Elfnote holds 1.0% and sits in Tier 1.

items.q: How much does going first matter?
items.md: Going first wins 53.5% of games on the TCG ladder and 56.8% in Genesys.

items.q: How often is the tier list updated?
items.md: Every week, on this same page. Each week also gets its own [meta report](/wiki/yu-gi-oh-meta-report-october-30-2026), and the [statistics page](/statistics) shows the current numbers for TCG and [Genesys](/statistics?ladder=genesys) between updates.

items.q: Where can I see decklists for these decks?
items.md: The [statistics page](/statistics) has sample decklists, card usage and full matchup tables for each deck.
